players.product: 22/28nm and mature-node logic foundry; silicon interposers

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F customer concentration: UMC's top ten customers accounted for 62.0%, 55.6% and 57.0% of operating revenues in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and its largest customer from the wafer fabrication segment for 13.1%, 10.4% and 11.8%; the only customer listed at 10% or more in 2024 and 2025, Customer A, generated NT$28,005,843 thousand of operating revenues in 2025 (NT$24,180,535 thousand in 2024). UMC names its primary customers as integrated device manufacturers such as Texas Instruments and Intel plus fabless design companies such as MediaTek, Realtek and Novatek, and says it is not dependent on any single customer. Accounts receivable from the top ten customers were 61% of total accounts receivable at December 31, 2025 (66% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: top ten customers 57.0% of 2025 operating revenues (55.6% in 2024); largest customer 11.8% (10.4% in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F revenue mix: wafer sales by application in 2025 were communication 41.4% (42.1% in 2024), consumer 30.6% (28.4%), computer 11.6% (13.5%) and others 16.4% (16.0%); by customer type, fabless design companies 80.9% (84.3% in 2024) and integrated device manufacturers 19.1% (15.7%). 28nm and below technologies contributed approximately 36.8% of foundry revenue in 2025 (33.7% in 2024, 30.7% in 2023).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 wafer sales: communication 41.4%, consumer 30.6%, computer 11.6%; 28nm and below 36.8% of foundry revenue

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F FY2025 results: operating revenues were NT$237,553,199 thousand (US$7,572,623 thousand) versus NT$232,302,584 thousand in 2024, of which wafer revenue NT$227,595,224 thousand (NT$221,820,412 thousand in 2024); gross margin 29.0% (32.6% in 2024), operating margin 18.5% (22.2%), net income NT$40,178,813 thousand. Research and development spending was NT$17,725 million (US$565 million), 7.5% of operating revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 operating revenues NT$237,553,199 thousand (NT$232,302,584 thousand in 2024); gross margin 29.0%

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F capacity: UMC's total estimated capacity was 5,163 thousand 12-inch wafer equivalents in 2025 (5,022 thousand in 2024) against actual output of 3,885 thousand (3,451 thousand), an average capacity utilization of 75.2% (68.7% in 2024, 68.5% in 2023). Fab 12A in Tainan (0.13 to 0.014 micron) is the largest at 1,629 thousand 12-inch equivalents of estimated annual capacity in 2025, followed by Fab 12i (684 thousand), Fab 12M (471 thousand) and Fab 12X (347 thousand); estimated full capacity at December 31, 2025 was 136,279 wafers per month at Fab 12A. UMC says its future capacity expansion plans will focus on 12-inch wafer facilities.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capacity 5,163 thousand 12-inch equivalents; output 3,885 thousand; average utilization 75.2% (68.7% in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F capex and commitments: capital expenditures were approximately NT$50,562 million (US$1,612 million) in 2025 versus NT$91,052 million in 2024 and NT$94,087 million in 2023, primarily to purchase equipment for research and development and production. UMC says its expansion projects will be supported by customers who have signed multi-year supply agreements; construction contracts amounted to NT$24,191 million (US$771 million) at December 31, 2025, of which approximately NT$5,454 million (US$174 million) was not yet recognized. Guarantee deposits, which mainly consisted of deposits of capacity reservation, were NT$39,805,928 thousand (non-current) at December 31, 2025, and UMC has wafer fabrication contracts under which it shall provide agreed production capacity to customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex NT$50,562 million (US$1,612 million) vs NT$91,052 million in 2024; construction contracts NT$24,191 million

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F supplier disclosure: UMC says it purchased a majority of its silicon wafers from Shin-Etsu Handotai Corporation, GlobalWafers, Sumco Group and Soitec, the principal makers of its wafers, and has signed long-term supply contracts with its suppliers to obtain sufficient quantities of raw materials; a small number of these suppliers hold an important position in its raw material supply.

20-F: UMC's development collaboration contract with Intel for a 12nm semiconductor process platform runs from January 25, 2024 to January 24, 2034, and the parties granted each other IP licenses. In 2025 Intel completed the technology transfer based on UMC's electrical design rules and UMC-verified process, replicating UMC's 12nm FinFET process; qualification of the technology transfer is being accelerated at Intel's Arizona fab and is expected to be completed in 2026, with production of the 12nm FinFET process expected to begin in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: contract January 25, 2024 to January 24, 2034; qualification at Intel's Arizona fab expected 2026; 12nm production from 2027

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F: in December 2025 UMC signed an MOU with Polar Semiconductor, LLC to explore collaboration on delivering scalable U.S.-based 8-inch production of wafers for industries including automotive, data centers, consumer electronics and aerospace and defense.
